introduction: Until the 1960s, most Indian banks were controlled by private business houses. They primarily lent to large industrialists and completely ignored agriculture and rural sectors ('Class Banking'). To shift to 'Mass Banking', then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi took historic steps.

core_concepts.title: The First Phase of Nationalization (1969)
core_concepts.description: Date: July 19, 1969. The government abruptly nationalized '14 major commercial banks' whose total deposits exceeded 'Rs. 50 crores'. Objective: To expand credit access to agriculture, small-scale industries, and rural areas.

core_concepts.title: The Second Phase of Nationalization (1980)
core_concepts.description: Date: April 15, 1980. The government nationalized '6 more commercial banks'. This time, the criterion was that the bank's deposits must exceed 'Rs. 200 crores'. This brought the total number of nationalized banks to 20.

core_concepts.title: The 1993 Merger (New Bank of India)
core_concepts.description: One of the 6 banks nationalized in 1980, the 'New Bank of India', suffered heavy losses. In 1993, the government merged it into the 'Punjab National Bank (PNB)'. Consequently, the number of nationalized banks dropped from 20 to 19 (excluding SBI).

core_concepts.title: Lead Bank Scheme (1969)
core_concepts.description: Introduced by the RBI shortly after the first nationalization (based on the Gadgil Study Group). Under this scheme, one specific bank in every district is designated as the 'Lead Bank', making it responsible for coordinating the overall financial development of that particular district.

important_entities.name: The Core Reason for Nationalization
important_entities.significance: The biggest outcome of nationalization was forcing banks to allocate a fixed percentage of their total loans (currently 40%) to agriculture, education, housing, and weaker sections. This mandate is known as Priority Sector Lending.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Technically, when exams refer to the 'Nationalized Banks list' of 1969 and 1980 (the 14+6 banks), SBI is NOT included in that list. SBI was nationalized much earlier under a special parliamentary act (SBI Act 1955). Therefore, SBI is a 'Public Sector Bank' (PSB), but not categorized under the 1969/80 nationalized group.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Memorize the strict criteria limits: 1969 required Rs. 50 crore deposits; 1980 required Rs. 200 crore deposits.

exam_strategy_tips: Dates are critical here: Memorize July 19, 1969 (Phase 1) and April 15, 1980 (Phase 2). Prime Minister: Indira Gandhi.
